Julian — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, then details below.

- Operational notification support: We aim to provide initial triage and customer-facing notification guidance within 24 hours of an incident being validated (T0 = detection by our IR team). For EU-impact incidents where regulatory notification may apply, we will prioritize and aim to provide a suggested notification package within 48–72 hours, including recommended customer wording and an evidence index.
- Log slices & retention: Application request logs and control-plane audit trails are retained for 90 days in primary storage; we maintain a searchable index for 365 days. We can produce time-bounded exports (UTC) for the 90-day primary window as CSV/JSON bundles. For older windows up to 365 days, exports are possible but may require additional processing time (48–72 hours).
- Cross-border restrictions: We do not withhold raw operational logs for lawful regulatory review. If a jurisdiction requires data residency constraints, we will coordinate with you to provide redacted extracts or a controlled remote review in a EU-only environment where feasible.

I am attaching a short evidence matrix and an example log export (redacted) for your review. Marcus and Kimberly — looping you both for legal/IR confirmation.

Best,

Julian — quick legal note to make the operational SLA explicit for contract language:

- "Initial customer notification support" = Redwood will provide an incident summary and recommended customer-facing notification language within 24–72 hours of confirmed incident detection, depending on triage complexity.
- "Evidence package" = Redwood will deliver an indexed package containing (1) incident timeline, (2) scope summary, (3) search export of application/access logs for the requested window (up to 90 days) in CSV/JSON, and (4) a list of retained artifacts and custody notes, delivered via secure share. We recommend customers allow a 72‑hour evidence fulfillment window for requests requiring manual redaction or extended retention exports.

Also flagging: if Acme requests copies of raw PII-containing request payloads for EU DPAs, we'll need a DPA-approved legal request or a signed Data Subject Access Protocol before release. We can do controlled review sessions instead.

Adding operational detail from IR side:

- Retention specifics: 90 days (hot) for full logs; 365-day index for metadata. For a forensic slice, we typically produce:
  * request_log_YYYYMMDD_HHMM-YYYYMMDD_HHMM.csv (application request details, non-PII redacted by default)
  * access_audit_YYYYMMDD.csv (control-plane actions)
  * kv-cache-checksums.txt (if relevant)

- Export process: Submit a signed evidence request to sec-requests@redwoodinference.com with the UTC start/end window and justification. For standard windows within 90 days we can deliver within 24–48 hours; for >90 days or cross-account whole-day exports expect 72 hours.
- Chain of custody: All artifacts delivered over our secure share include checksums and a manifest; we log downloads to the request ticket.

Julian — if you can send the exact UTC window you need and whether you need raw request payloads or redacted extracts, we'll queue this as HS-98765 and start the export.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Incident Response, Redwood Inference
